title: 1.3 Projectile motion: horizontal and inclined launches

q.Q1: Q1. Two identical stones leave a cliff at the same time: one is dropped, the other thrown horizontally. Explain why they hit the level ground at the same time.

q.Q2: Q2. A food bag is dropped from a plane flying horizontally at 50 m/s at a height of 180 m. Find (a) the time to reach the ground, (b) the horizontal distance travelled (g = 10 m/s2).
q.Q3: Q3. Why must the pilot release the bag before the plane is directly above the target?

q.Q4: Q4. A ball is kicked at 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. Find (a) the vertical and horizontal components of velocity, (b) the time of flight (g = 10 m/s2).
q.Table: Q5. Which angle of projection gives the greatest range on level ground (same speed)?

q.Q6: Q6. State the velocity of a projectile at the highest point of its path and explain.

q.Q7: Q7. A javelin is thrown at 25 m/s. Calculate its maximum possible range on level ground and the angle needed (g = 10 m/s2, ignore air resistance).

q.Exit ticket: Exit ticket. Which component of a projectile's velocity stays constant, and why?
